heard: An imperial commander threw his sword and made the tide vanish. In May 1333, Nitta Yashasada besieged Kamakura. Seven mountain passes contained guarded checkpoints. Western passes had rows of wooden shielding. Chronicles state he threw his sword and the sea parted. Analysis indicates he timed a low tide. Forces breached the capital ending Shogunate rule. An imperial commander threw his sword and made the tide vanish.
